environment.docker: pebble runs as a container for Part B only
environment.note: This is a TLS-behavior and ACME-protocol capability check, not a timing benchmark. Part A is fully deterministic (local OpenSSL, no network). Part B drives a real ACME state machine against a local pebble CA; the numbers it returns (144h lifetime, window widths) are pebble defaults, not Let's Encrypt policy.

subject.name: short-lived-cert renewal (expiry semantics + ACME ARI)

components.openssl: 3.5.6 (Part A local CA + leaf + TLS probe)
components.acme_client: hand-written pure-Python ACME (ES256 JWS, cryptography 48, no acme/certbot lib)

subject.note: pebble was pulled as :latest at run time (2026-06-23) — NOT version-pinned. This is a real limitation: re-running today pulls a newer pebble and the exact lifetime/window may drift. The mechanism under test (ARI wire format, CertID derivation, shortlived-profile ordering) follows draft-ietf-acme-ari-03, now finalized as RFC 9773, and is stable across pebble versions; the specific 144h/window numbers are not.

baseline.name: long-lived certificate + calendar/cron renewal
baseline.note: Compared conceptually in the post (why a fixed cron date silently inverts meaning once certs get short). No long-lived-cert path was executed as a measured baseline; the contrast is by capability, not by measured timing.

cross_reference.real_ca_numbers: NOT measured. The 2026-03 -> 2029 industry timeline (398d -> 47d) and Let's Encrypt's real short-lived profile lifetimes/windows are cited from the CA/B Forum + Let's Encrypt announcements, explicitly flagged as not-firsthand. Only pebble's default (144h) was observed here.
cross_reference.dcv_failures: NOT measured. Part B ran pebble with PEBBLE_VA_ALWAYS_VALID=1, which auto-satisfies domain validation. Real DCV failure modes are abstracted by Part A's 'renewal stalled' case: whatever the cause, once NotAfter passes the outcome is identical (hard handshake failure).

data_source.name: pebble (local test CA)
data_source.drift_warning: pebble is a test server, not Let's Encrypt. The lifetime (144h) and suggestedWindow widths in results.json are pebble defaults captured on 2026-06-23. They demonstrate the ARI mechanism, not production CA policy. pebble was not version-pinned (:latest); re-running may surface a different build.

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: harness + captured logs committed; per-run generated keys/certs discarded
raw_artifacts.note: Part A generates throwaway EC keys, a 1-day local root CA, and short-lived leaf certs on every run (ca.key/ca.crt/leaf.*). These are non-deterministic (fresh keys + wall-clock validity each run) and are intentionally NOT committed, same rationale as a non-deterministic screenshot. The committed evidence is the harness (run.sh, tls_probe.py, acme_ari.py) plus the captured run logs (partA/probe-result.txt, partB/acme-ari-result.txt) from 2026-06-23. See checksums.txt for integrity hashes of the committed files.
